description: Replace the per-panel cuBLAS strided-batched trailing GEMMs (n=512/1024, ~30-48% of time) with CUTLASS GROUPED/batched GEMM to cut the per-panel host launch count. Currently each of the n/nb panels issues separate torch.bmm calls (W=V^T C; C-=V T^T W) plus the per-matrix TF32/FP32 split — many small launches. CUTLASS grouped GEMM (KernelPtrArrayTmaWarpSpecialized, sm_100, GemmUniversalMode::kGrouped) does variable-per-group GEMMs in ONE launch across the whole batch, and supports per-group precision so the well(TF32)/ill(FP32) split can be expressed without a host gather/reorder. This is a library-substitution distinct from removing the host classify sync; it attacks the trailing GEMM launch overhead directly. Build against stock CUTLASS bundled with torch if available, else a custom batched-GEMM kernel that fuses the two trailing GEMMs + the V/T apply into one launch per panel. Keep panel FP32, n!=512/1024 as parent. Avoid the substring 'stream' incl. comments (CUTLASS warp-specialized is fine; just no non-default CUDA queue and no 'stream' text).

Trial 1: fused tensor-core (wmma 16x16x8 tf32) per-matrix-routed trailing kernel trailing_mma; one launch applies the whole trailing update for n=512/1024 routing TF32(well)/FP32(ill) in-kernel from a device flag (no host argsort/gather/inverse-permute, no .item sync). Builds clean. VALIDATION FAIL: n=1024 clustered (all-well) residual 1.37e29 (wmma C-update layout bug) + n=512/1024 mixed H NaN/Inf. Mechanism wired; debugging the wmma fragment layout next.

Trial 1 (corrected): fused tensor-core (wmma 16x16x8 tf32) per-matrix-routed trailing kernel trailing_mma, applied to the WHOLE n=512/1024 routed path. CORRECT: 22 tests PASS + offgrid/invariance/diff_correctness guards ALL CLEAN (in-kernel routing handles every batch composition/position without reorder). PERF REGRESSION: contention-invariant (unchanged sentinels shape0=32.9us, shape5=47730us, shape6=101979us all match the parent run) the changed n=512/1024 shapes are 2.3-2.8x SLOWER: shape3 n512-dense 74017 vs parent 26595us, shape7 n512-mixed 80888 vs 32536us, shape4 n1024 75646 vs 32171us. The hand-rolled wmma trailing GEMM (one CTA per matrix x 64-col tile, 4 warps, serial K-loop re-staging V/C per chunk) cannot match cuBLAS's tuned cutlass s256x256tf32gemm tensor-core kernel; the ~600us launch+reorder savings are swamped. Matches the brief's prior (in-kernel wmma ~1.37x slower; brief 27 scalar 9x). geomean 22921us (contended) vs parent ~13200us same-contention. NEXT: restrict the fused kernel to ONLY the mixed path (where the reorder actually lives); all-well/all-ill stay on cuBLAS.

Trial 2: restrict trailing_mma to the MIXED (heterogeneous) path only; all-well->cuBLAS TF32 bmm, all-ill->cuBLAS FP32 bmm (both unchanged from parent, no reorder). Validate PASS. Contention-invariant confirmation: shapes 3/4/9/10/11 reverted to EXACT parent values (26607/32164/26475/26602/32099us) and sentinels 0/5/6 match parent run -- so ONLY mixed changed. Mixed STILL regresses 2.6x: shape7 n512-mixed 85515 vs parent 32536us, shape8 n1024-mixed 98889 vs 38321us. The reorder+sync the fused kernel removes (~448us gather + radix-sort + .item) is tiny vs the GEMM, which the hand-rolled wmma does ~2.6x slower than cuBLAS s256x256tf32gemm. geomean 15535us (contended) vs parent ~13200us. CLEAR NEGATIVE for replacing the trailing GEMM. NEXT: try to make the wmma GEMM itself faster (bigger per-warp output tiles, K double-buffer) -- but cuBLAS is hard to beat; may confirm the negative.

Trial 3: faster wmma C-update (each warp owns all TN cols over its row-blocks; reuse staged-V A-fragment; b_frag loaded DIRECTLY from Ysh in SMEM, no per-chunk B restage). Math correct on random well matrices (relmax 1e-3). But VALIDATION FAIL via diff_correctness guard: removing the tf32_round (round-nearest-even) pre-rounding from the C-update let wmma's HW mantissa TRUNCATION push dense-but-TF32-marginal matrices over budget -- matrix 633 (rankdef+mixed seed 776057, row_dr=1.95 density=1.0 => classifier says WELL) scaled factor residual 26.5>20 on TF32 but 0.04 on FP32. The parent cuBLAS TF32 path passes because cuBLAS TF32 is more accurate than a truncating hand-rolled wmma. Confirms the custom kernel can't match cuBLAS on accuracy either. NEXT: re-add RNE rounding to restore trial-2 accuracy, then clean-benchmark the throughput-improved version.

Trial 4: faster wmma C-update (row-block split, direct Ysh B-load) + RNE tf32_round restored on V/Y for the well path -> VALID (22 tests + offgrid/invariance/diff_correctness ALL CLEAN; matrix-633 boundary case now passes). Benchmark in a LESS-contended run (geomean 11057us; sentinels shape5=31877, shape6=68030 vs parent-run 48422/102329 confirm lower contention, so compare RATIOS not raw). Contention-invariant: shape7 n512-mixed(my fused kernel)/shape9 n512-rankdef(reverted to cuBLAS)=71426/17536=4.07x; parent's same ratio=32536/26460=1.23x => the fused mixed path is ~3.3x SLOWER than cuBLAS relative to the same-run dense baseline. Root cause: the ill(FP32) C-update is a naive per-thread scalar dot loop (no tensor cores), far slower than cuBLAS cutlass_80_simt_sgemm; the well wmma also trails cutlass s256x256tf32gemm. Faster C-update helped the well half but the ill half + the wmma-vs-cuBLAS gap dominate. CLEAR NEGATIVE confirmed across the well, ill, and mixed groups.

Trial 5 (diagnostic, cleanest head-to-head): route the homogeneous ALL-WELL n=512/1024 batches through the improved fused tensor-core kernel too (no reorder/sync to save here => pure GEMM-vs-cuBLAS). Contention-invariant (sentinels shape0=32.86us, shape5=47624us, shape6=100928us match the parent's higher-contention run exactly): all-well shape3 n512-dense=93347 vs parent cuBLAS 26595us => 3.51x SLOWER; shape9 rankdef=93227 vs 26460 => 3.52x; shape4 n1024=93107 vs 32171 => 2.89x; shape11=93093 vs 32116 => 2.90x. So the hand-rolled wmma trailing GEMM is 2.9-3.5x slower than cuBLAS's cutlass3x_sm100_tensorop_s256x256/s128x128 tf32gemm EVEN AFTER the data-reuse rewrite, on shapes with ZERO reorder to save. DEFINITIVE NEGATIVE: cuBLAS bmm already dispatches the optimal CUTLASS sm_100 tensor-core kernels (confirmed in every n512 profile), so neither a custom wmma kernel nor a CUTLASS grouped GEMM (which uses the SAME kernels) can beat it; the launch/reorder savings (~448us gather+sort+sync, ~1-2%) are dwarfed. geomean 26252us (contended). Reverting final state to the least-regressing fused config (mixed-only) for handoff.

Trial 6 (final handoff): mixed-only fused kernel (_WELL_TRAILING=bmm so all-well->cuBLAS per trial 5; _MIXED_TRAILING=mma). Validate PASS + offgrid/invariance/diff_correctness ALL CLEAN. Contention-invariant (sentinels shape0=32.9, shape3=26606, shape5=47642, shape6=101965 match parent's higher-contention run): non-mixed shapes reverted to EXACT parent cuBLAS; mixed shape7 n512=107192/shape9 n512=26467 ratio=4.05x vs parent 1.23x => mixed still ~3.3x slower. geomean 16076us vs parent ~13200us same-contention -- a regression confined to the 2 mixed shapes. This is the least-regressing fused-kernel config; the brief's core lever (replace the cuBLAS trailing GEMM with a custom/CUTLASS-grouped batched GEMM) is a measured NEGATIVE: cuBLAS bmm already dispatches optimal CUTLASS sm_100 tensor-core kernels, so neither path can beat it, and the launch/reorder savings (~1-2%) are dwarfed.

Brief 33 (replace per-panel cuBLAS trailing GEMMs with CUTLASS grouped / custom batched GEMM): exhaustively explored, MEASURED NEGATIVE for both paths. PATH 1 (CUTLASS grouped GEMM) is REMOTE-UNSAFE here: torch bundles NO C++ CUTLASS (only the nvidia_cutlass_dsl Python DSL + ATen-internal cutlass_common.cuh; torch declares no cutlass dep). Full CUTLASS 4.5 with the Blackwell grouped example 75 exists only at the machine-local /opt/cutlass -> building against it would pass local validate but FAIL the remote leaderboard build (the documented BF16x9-class trap). AND the parent n512 profile shows cuBLAS bmm ALREADY dispatches the optimal CUTLASS sm_100 tensor-core kernels (cutlass3x_sm100_tensorop_s256x256/s128x128 tf32gemm for well, cutlass_80_simt_sgemm for ill) -- a grouped GEMM would use the SAME kernels, so it cannot be faster for our uniform-per-class shapes (grouped's edge is variable per-group shapes, which we don't have); its only structural win (fewer launches on the mixed split) saves the same ~1-2% the custom path already removes. PATH 2 (custom fused tensor-core batched kernel, the brief's fallback): BUILT and CORRECT -- trailing_mma applies the whole C:=(I-V T^T V^T)C for all matrices in ONE launch, routing TF32(well, wmma 16x16x8)/FP32(ill) per-matrix in-kernel from a device flag, NO host argsort/gather/inverse-permute, NO .item sync. 22 tests PASS + offgrid/invariance/diff_correctness ALL CLEAN. But it REGRESSES on speed at every setting (contention-invariant ratios vs same-run cuBLAS dense baseline): trial5 clean all-well head-to-head shape3 93347 vs parent cuBLAS 26595 = 3.51x SLOWER (n1024 2.89x) -- on shapes with ZERO reorder to save, pure GEMM-vs-cuBLAS; trial4/6 mixed-only shape7/shape9 ratio 4.05x vs parent 1.23x = ~3.3x slower. The wmma trailing GEMM is 2.9-3.5x slower than cuBLAS's tuned cutlass tf32gemm EVEN AFTER a data-reuse rewrite (row-block-split warps, b_frag loaded direct from SMEM Y, staged-V reuse cut redundant global reads), and the ill FP32 C-update is a naive scalar loop far slower than cuBLAS cutlass_80_simt_sgemm. The launch+reorder savings the brief targets (~448us gather + radix-sort + .item sync, ~1-2% of the n512 shape) are dwarfed by the GEMM throughput loss. PROGRESSION: T1 whole-path fused (after fixing a cb=32 wmma A-tile staging bug) 2.78x slower; T2 mixed-only 2.6x; T3 faster C-update but tf32 TRUNCATION (vs RNE) pushed a TF32-marginal dense matrix (633: row_dr 1.95, density 1.0 => classifier WELL, but scaled resid 26.5>20 on TF32, 0.04 FP32) over the factor gate -> diff_correctness FLAGGED; T4 re-added RNE tf32_round on V/Y -> VALID; T5 diagnostic all-well 3.5x; T6 handoff=mixed-only (least-regressing, geomean 16076 vs parent ~13200 same-contention). FINAL STATE: mixed-only fused kernel wired+committed (non-mixed reverted to cuBLAS, which trial 5 proved is 3.5x faster than the custom kernel). HANDOFF PROFILE saved (brief-33-trial-6-n512dense-dd104e672.nsys-rep, identical to parent: panel 63.8%, cuBLAS tf32gemm ~30%). OPEN directions I did NOT close (remote-safe, could net positive): (a) HYBRID mixed path -- keep cuBLAS TF32 bmm on the WHOLE batch (one launch, no reorder) and OVERWRITE only the ~156 ill matrices' trailing per-panel with a custom FP32 kernel from a snapshot of their pre-update C (avoids the full-batch gather/sort while keeping cuBLAS's fast tensor-core GEMM for the bulk; cost = redundant cuBLAS-on-ill + a small ill-only snapshot, EV uncertain, untried); (b) the launch-count win is genuinely small here (the per-panel bmm calls are large GEMMs, well-amortized) so the bigger n512/1024 lever remains the PANEL (62-64% of every n512 shape, not the trailing GEMM) -- briefs 23/29 (CholeskyQR2-HR / TSQR-HR to put the panel on tensor cores) attack the real bottleneck; (c) if a future torch ships C++ CUTLASS or the remote env is confirmed to have /opt/cutlass, grouped GEMM could fold the mixed well/ill split into one launch, but it still can't out-GEMM cuBLAS. RECOMMENDATION: this lever (custom/grouped trailing GEMM) does not beat cuBLAS; redirect workers to the panel-factorization bottleneck or the hybrid-mixed reorder-elimination (a) that keeps cuBLAS's GEMM.
